verdict.reasoning: Headache location, timing, and character are supported, but ‘severe’ is overstated: patient reports left-sided headache starting ~4 hours ago with abrupt onset and current intensity 5–6/10. Transcript: “about four hours ago, You've developed a headache on the left side of the head” and pain “maybe five. Well, six.”
The headache came on suddenly. Transcript: Doctor asks, “Was it a sudden onset headache? Did it come on suddenly?” Patient: “Yeah, yeah, yeah.” and “It came like kind of suddenly.”
Pain score documented as 5–6/10. Transcript: “maybe five. Well, six. … Doctor: Six probably.”
Visual disturbance described as blurred vision with zigzag lines. Transcript: “My vision is quite blurred… Like some zigzag lines kind of.”
Dizziness is reported with the headache. Transcript: “So it started in the morning. I feel like dizzy. My vision is a little bit blue flourish.”
Movement worsens symptoms. Transcript: “when I move like the thing is that if I leave bed I start to feel like even worse if I move. So I just want to have my head like really not moving.”
Screens are poorly tolerated. Transcript: “I feel a little bit. A little bit. I cannot stand screens.”
Two episodes of vomiting and ongoing nausea are reported; persistent vomiting is not claimed. Transcript: “I vomit twice, actually… And I still feel nausea. I'm about to vomit very soon, I think.”

Paracetamol was taken about 3 hours before consult (1 hour after onset) without benefit. Transcript: “the headache started like… four hours ago… maybe three hours ago because I couldn't stand it.” and “I tried paracetamol but didn't work. To be honest. I feel exactly the same.”
Patient denies limb weakness. Transcript: Doctor: “Have you noticed any weakness in your arms or legs?” Patient: “No, not it. No. No.”

Patient denies gait disturbance. Transcript: Doctor: “when you're walking, you're able to walk fine in a straight line, or is your walk… funny?” Patient: “Not really.” and later doctor summarizes: “you're walking fine.”
History of kidney stones is explicitly mentioned. Transcript: “Well, I had the kidney stone” and doctor: “You've mentioned in the past you've had kidney stones.”
No regular medications. Transcript: Doctor: “Do you take any regular medications?” Patient: “No.”
Paracetamol taken today for this headache. Transcript: “Yeah, I tried paracetamol but didn't work.” and timing: “maybe three hours ago.”
No known drug allergies. Transcript: Doctor: “Are you allergic to any medications?” Patient: “Not that I'm aware. Yeah, not that I'm aware.”
Maternal history of migraine. Transcript: “My mother has migraines.” and confirmed again: “You said. You mentioned your mother has migraines.”
Mother has hypothyroidism. Transcript: “also, I have hypothyroidism in the family” and clarified: “She also has hypothyroidism.”
Pregnancy is doubted/essentially denied. Transcript: Doctor: “Is there any chance you could be pregnant?” Patient: “I really doubt it.”

Beyond headache-related symptoms, other systems are effectively negative (no limb weakness, no gait change; no other systemic complaints mentioned). Under the rule for implicit negatives, summarizing ROS as otherwise unremarkable is acceptable. Transcript: denials of weakness and gait change and no other ROS positives documented.

Doctor assesses presentation as migraine and it is the first such episode. Transcript: Doctor: “it sounds like what you're suffering from is what's known as a migraine.” Patient: “I never had it.” Headache is unilateral with visual disturbance, nausea, and vomiting as described earlier.

Health anxiety about serious brain pathology is evident. Transcript: Patient: “I'm a little bit hypochondriac… this can be some kind of brain tumor or something… Or maybe a stroke… you definitely start to wonder if I should go to A and E urgently… I might really have something serious.”

Plan includes ibuprofen, anti-sickness medication, and sugary carbonated drink. Transcript: “I would recommend… maybe something like ibuprofen.” and “ibuprofen with an anti sickness which you can get from the pharmacy. And also to drink a sugary carbonated drink, something like coke.”

Migraleve is mentioned but triptans are not. Transcript: “Then we can go up the treatment ladder. You can get specific migraleve medication.” There is no mention of a “triptan-containing agent,” so stating that as part of the plan adds unsupported detail.

A same-day in-person assessment for full neurological exam is planned. Transcript: “we would want to see you as soon as possible to do like a full neurological exam as well… we could see you today at some point.”

No explicit advice about ED attendance for red-flag features is documented. Transcript only: “Any further problems between now and your appointment, please do let us know.” No mention of ED, sudden worsening, neurological deficit, vision loss, or intractable pain/vomiting.

Doctor explains migraine nature/course and offers reassurance and plan. Transcript includes education on timing of migraine onset in life and features, plus a management plan and opportunity for questions: “So usually with migraines, they can present at different times in people lives… The reason why this sounds like migraines is because…” This constitutes education and implicit reassurance.
Patient may cancel appointment if improved. Transcript: “if you do take these medications and… you feel much better on yourself, you can cancel it. You can give us a call and cancel it.”

Follow-up same-day in-person review for neurological exam is arranged. Transcript: “we would want to see you as soon as possible to do like a full neurological exam… we could see you today at some point.”

No ED-specific or detailed red-flag instructions are given. Transcript only advises to contact the practice: “Any further problems between now and your appointment, please do let us know.” No mention of emergency department or specific triggers like neurological deficits or vision loss.
Patient is allowed to cancel the appointment if better. Transcript: “if… you feel much better on yourself, you can cancel it. You can give us a call and cancel it.”
